On November 5, 2012, China's 29th Antarctic scientific expedition team set out. On December 16, the team members went to Kunlun Station located at Dome A for investigation. The following figure is a schematic diagram of part of Antarctica. Read the figure and answer the question.

<image1>

On a certain day, scientific expedition team members at Zhongshan Station (about 76°E) found that the sun was on the horizon on the west side of the Amery Ice Shelf. Two hours later, they found that the sun was again on the horizon on the other side. Then what was the approximate Beijing time at this time?

The two times are separated by 2 hours, so the second observation is 1 hour after local solar midnight, that is, the local solar time at Zhongshan Station is about 1:00. Beijing time uses the zone time of 120°E. Zhongshan Station is about 76°E, differing from the central meridian of the Beijing time zone, 120°E, by 44°. The time difference is 44×4 minutes=176 minutes=2 hours 56 minutes, and 120°E is east of 76°E, so Beijing time is 2 hours 56 minutes earlier than Zhongshan Station local time. On November 5, 2012, China's 29th Antarctic scientific expedition team set out. On December 16, the team members went to Kunlun Station located at Dome A for investigation. The following figure is a schematic diagram of part of Antarctica. Read the figure and answer the question.

<image1>

On a certain day, scientific expedition team members at Zhongshan Station (about 76°E) found that the sun was on the horizon on the west side of the Amery Ice Shelf. Two hours later, they found that the sun was again on the horizon on the other side. Then what was the approximate Beijing time at this time?

method.method_draft: First describe the map: Zhongshan Station is plotted near the Amery Ice Shelf, in the Antarctic region, with longitude lines around 70°E–80°E. Use Zhongshan's longitude as about 76°E. The two horizon observations are 2 hours apart and occur on opposite sides, so take their midpoint as local solar midnight at Zhongshan. Therefore the second observation is 1 hour after local midnight, i.e. local solar time about 1:00. Convert from 76°E local solar time to Beijing time at 120°E: Beijing is ahead by (120−76)×4 minutes = 176 minutes = 2 h 56 min. Thus 1:00 + 2:56 = 3:56.
